from.place: Integral exceptional-adjoint proof, paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation; technical foundations for the finite-adjunction-diagram realization, specifically the full functor-category pushout comparison in lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization. Technical input: Cartesian simplicial model of marked simplicial sets over a point. Foundational sublemma: Marked-anodyne lifting, products and mapping objects. Auxiliary Proposition 3.1.1.5: replacement of final marked horns by endpoint-boundary prisms in the generator calculation.

title: Final marked horns and endpoint prisms generate the same class
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A marked simplicial set is a simplicial set with a subset of its edges containing all degenerate edges; maps preserve these edges. Products mark an edge exactly when both its coordinates are marked. Write $K^\flat$ and $K^\sharp$ for the minimal and full markings. For a family $S$ of marked maps let $\langle S\rangle$ be its closure together with isomorphisms under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts. A transfinite composition is indexed by a small ordinal and takes colimits at limit stages; a retract is in the arrow category. Let $I$ consist of $(\Lambda_i^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$ for $0<i<n$. Let $F$ consist of $(\Lambda_n^n,E\cap(\Lambda_n^n)_1)\to(\Delta^n,E)$ for $n>0$, where $E$ is the degenerate edges and $[n-1,n]$. For every simplicial monomorphism $h:A\hookrightarrow B$, define
$$ P(h):((\Delta^1)^\sharp\times A^\flat)\amalg_{\{1\}^\sharp\times A^\flat}(\{1\}^\sharp\times B^\flat)\longrightarrow(\Delta^1)^\sharp\times B^\flat. $$
For $m\geq1$, let $\partial\Delta^m$ be the union of all proper faces of $\Delta^m$. Let $P_\partial=\{P(\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m):m\geq0\}$ with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, and let $P_{\mathrm{mono}}$ be the family of $P(h)$ for all small simplicial monomorphisms. Then
$$\langle I\cup F\rangle=\langle I\cup P_\partial\rangle=\langle I\cup P_{\mathrm{mono}}\rangle.$$
In particular every $P(h)$ belongs to $\langle I\cup F\rangle$.
